source.author: verg
source.text: Ego te, quae plurima fando enumerare vales, numquam, regina, negabo promeritam; nec me meminisse pigebit Elissae, dum memor ipse mei, dum spiritus hos regit artus.
source.text_original: 'Ego te, quae plurima fando / enumerare vales, numquam, regina, negabo / promeritam; nec me meminisse pigebit Elissae, / dum memor ipse mei, dum spiritus hos regit artus.
source.text_english: I shall never deny, queen, that you have well earned my gratitude, you who can recount so many things in speaking; nor shall I ever be ashamed to remember Elissa, so long as I myself remember myself, so long as breath rules these limbs.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: intendamus ergo iustitiae, quae nos inseparabilis comes ad deum sola perducet, et dum spiritus hos regit artus, infatigabilem militiam deo militemus , stationes celebremus, congrediamur cum hoste quem fortiter, ut ac aduersario praemium uirtutis quod ipse promisit a domino consequamur.
reuse.text_original: intendamus ergo iustitiae, quae nos inseparabilis comes ad deum sola perducet, et dum spiritus hos regit artus, infatigabilem militiam deo militemus , stationes celebremus, congrediamur cum hoste quem fortiter, ut ac aduersario praemium uirtutis quod ipse promisit a domino consequamur.
reuse.text_english: Let us therefore aim at justice, which alone, as our inseparable companion, will lead us to God; and while the spirit governs these limbs, let us serve God in tireless warfare, keep our watches, and join battle with the enemy, whom we must bravely overcome, so that we may obtain from the Lord the reward of virtue, which he himself has promised.
